title: lichen_radio_progress watchdog contract narrowed: idle-armed radio feeds no heartbeat; puck docs stale
description: Found by security+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (P2). The old RX thread bumped lichen_radio_progress() every loop pass (<=RX_TIMEOUT_MS), proving the radio path alive even during silence. The async RX (sb0b) bumps only on packet deliveries and successful arms - deliberately not on retry attempts, which masked wedges by keeping the heartbeat fresh. Net effect: while the radio sits idle and armed (the common case), nothing bumps the hook; puck's watchdog survives only because its main loop kicks every <=1s (apps/puck/src/main.c:542). The original purpose - keeping WDT fed while main blocks in a long network call - no longer holds, and the puck main.c comment block (main.c:226-255) still describes thread-poll semantics. Fix: either a low-rate keepalive work item while armed-and-idle (careful: reintroduces polling the 9hfe epic removed), or liveness sourced from driver IRQ counters, plus update puck's stall-contract comment. Related: a hung lora_send() (SPI fault) holds modem_mutex indefinitely and masks stalls from the watchdog - pre-existing shape.
